logline: A delinquent teenager with 50 consecutive rejections joins his high school basketball team to impress a girl, and discovers a genuine gift for the sport as his team chases a national championship.

renewal.note: The original 101-episode TV anime ran from October 1993 to March 1996. A theatrical film continuation, The First Slam Dunk (2022), directed by manga creator Takehiko Inoue, grossed over $281 million worldwide and is considered the canonical sequel.

bollymeter.basis: MAL score of 8.56 from a large voter base reflects enduring cult status; Anime News Network awarded episodes 25-60 an A- overall, praising its ability to tie coming-of-age storytelling with basketball beautifully.

pull_quotes.text: Ties together coming-of-age stories with basketball games beautifully.

seasons.review_body: Produced by Toei Animation and broadcast on TV Asahi from October 1993 to March 1996, Slam Dunk's 101-episode run is considered one of the foundational sports anime of its era. Critics who revisited the series on its Crunchyroll streaming release noted its ability to tie coming-of-age storytelling with basketball pacing in ways that hold up decades later. The series is credited with fuelling a genuine basketball boom among Japanese youth in the 1990s. Pacing issues and filler arcs are real - a consequence of the anime outrunning the manga - but the central emotional arc of Hanamichi Sakuragi's transformation from hot-headed delinquent to devoted athlete is consistently praised as earnest and effective. The MAL community score of 8.56 across a large voting base confirms sustained cross-generational appeal.

episode_reviews.title: Sakuragi Hanamichi, the Basketball Beginner
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere sets the hook fast: a towering, red-haired delinquent falls for a girl who loves basketball, and suddenly the sport means everything to him. The comedic energy and stubborn charm of Sakuragi are established in a single episode.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sakuragi declares he is a basketball genius - a claim the show will spend 101 episodes making true through sheer stubbornness.

episode_reviews.title: The Tip-Off of the Interhigh
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The national tournament arc begins in earnest. Years of character-building snap into focus as Shohoku face elite opposition for the first time. The stakes feel real because the show has taken its time earning them.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Shohoku team walks onto the Interhigh floor for the first time - the moment the show transitions from underdog comedy to genuine sports drama.
